<a id="layer-cr-5"></a>
## CR.5 — Logarithmic geometry and log-crystalline cohomology

*Coverage in the CR.5 part: planned. 24 nodes, 5 planets.*

The layer builds log crystalline cohomology on CR.5:log-algebra and the PD theory of CR.0, in two generalities: fine log schemes (Kato §§5–6) and integral quasi-coherent ones (Beilinson §§1.1–1.8, 1.17, Česnavičius–Koshikawa §5).

- **Log differentials.** The universal log derivation and Ω¹_log, the log de Rham complex with coefficients; the semistable chart formula, with Ω¹_log free of rank d − 1 relative to the log base; absolute residues along the components; behaviour under reduction and completion.
- **Cartier type.** Morphisms of Cartier type (integral with exact relative Frobenius) and the log Cartier isomorphism.
- **Envelopes and sites.** Exactification of closed immersions; fine log PD envelopes, for which the base PD structure must extend to the ambient scheme, and integral quasi-coherent ones; exact and PD smooth log PD thickenings; the log crystalline site with the étale topology; log crystals.
- **Connections and cohomology.** Log PD stratifications, integrable log connections and log quasi-nilpotence; the equivalence of crystals with modules with quasi-nilpotent integrable log connection on a log smooth embedding; the filtered log PD de Rham complex, the log Poincaré lemma and embedding-system descent; derived p-adic log crystalline cohomology as a derived limit of finite levels.
- **A_cris with its log structure.** The unique lift of a log structure whose characteristic is uniquely p-divisible, and the induced log structure on A_cris from the valuation log structure of O_C, which AInfCohomology AI.6 uses.

Structural proposal S14 moves the integral quasi-coherent branch into a sub-layer `CR.5:qc-crystalline`. The five planets are log differentials, Cartier type, log PD envelopes, the log crystalline site and the log Poincaré lemma.

**Still open in this layer.**

- Supply the generic ordinary PD envelope/canonical-base imports from CR.0 and completion interface.
- Apply the proposed Beilinson substage and AI.6 dependency; verify the complete O_C/A_cris chart-lift proof chain.
- Supply genuine ringed log PD site/crystal, joint-base PD and enhanced tower types; replace arbitrary-object equivalences and complete named PD/Cartier/descent tests.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-differentials"></a>
### Logarithmic differentials

`CR.5/log-differentials` · construction · planet “Logarithmic differentials” · part CR.5

For a prelog ring map (A,Q)→(B,P), Ω¹_log is (Ω¹_{B/A}⊕B⊗ℤP^gp) modulo dα(p)−α(p)⊗p and the images of Q^gp. Its maps d:B→Ω¹ and dlog:P→(Ω¹,+) represent pairs consisting of an A-derivation D and a monoid-to-additive-group map δ with Dα(p)=α(p)δ(p) and δ(Q)=0. Sheafify on log schemes. Logification leaves this module unchanged.

**Construction.**

1. Use the pinned ordinary Kähler differential module and the pinned groupification; neither is planned again.
2. Form the quotient by the two explicit relation families; verify the universal property and étale sheafification.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logDifferentials.dlog_mul` (simp): dlog(pq)=dlog(p)+dlog(q).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logDifferentials.d_alpha` (relation): d(α(p))=α(p)dlog(p).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logDifferentials.lift` (universal-property): Log derivation pairs correspond uniquely to B-linear maps from Ω¹_log.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logDifferentials.trivial_log` (compatibility): With trivial log structures Ω¹_log is the ordinary Kähler module.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logDifferentials.toric_line` (computation): For A[t] with t-chart over trivial A, Ω¹_log=A[t]dlog(t) and dt=t dlog(t).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logDifferentials.log_point` (non-example): The standard log point over the trivial log point has Ω¹_log=k, although Ω¹_{k/k}=0.

**Acceptance.**

- For a toric chart A[Q]→A[P], Ω¹_log=A[P]⊗ℤ(P^gp/Q^gp).

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-de-rham`](#n-cr-5-log-de-rham): The universal log derivation gives the degree-one differential and its generators; the relations identify relative semistable forms and the Leibniz rule for coefficient connections.
- kato §1.7–1.8, pp.195–196; logification invariance and base-change formula: The source construction uses the universal log derivation gives the degree-one differential and its generators; the relations identify relative semistable forms and the Leibniz rule for coefficient connections.

`CR.5/log-de-rham` · construction · part CR.5

<a id="n-cr-5-semistable-log-forms"></a>
### Semistable chart differential formula

`CR.5/semistable-log-forms` · theorem · part CR.5

Let A=O_K[x₁,…,x_d]/(x₁⋯x_r−π), 1≤r≤d, with base ℕ→O_K, 1↦π, and source ℕ^r, e_i↦x_i. Relative to this log base, Ω¹_log is (⊕_{i≤r}Ae_i⊕⊕_{j>r}A dx_j)/A(e₁+⋯+e_r), with dlog x_i=e_i and dx_i=x_i e_i. It is free of rank d−1. The exterior powers give the full relative log complex; the same formula holds continuously after adic completion with its inherited chart.

**Proof outline.**

1. Apply the quotient definition of log differentials to the diagonal chart.
2. The polynomial relation differentiates to πΣe_i and is already killed by the stronger log-base relation Σe_i=0.
3. Eliminate e_r to obtain the free basis, then pass to continuous forms by the specified completion.

**Acceptance.**

<a id="n-cr-5-semistable-residues"></a>
### Absolute semistable residue maps

`CR.5/semistable-residues` · construction · part CR.5

For the same semistable A, take log differentials relative to the trivial log structure on O_K, denoted Ω_abs, not relative to O_K^log. Here Ω_abs=(A^r⊕A^{d−r})/A(πΣe_i). For the component D_i=(x_i=0), define res_i:Ω_abs→A/(x_i) by res_i(e_j)=δ_ij and res_i(dx_j)=0 for j>r. It is well defined since π=0 on D_i. Individual res_i do not factor through Ω¹_{A/O_K^log}, since res_i(Σe_j)=1. Exterior residues use the corresponding component log forms and the signed wedge convention.

**Construction.**

1. Retain the absolute relation πΣe_i instead of killing Σe_i.
2. Define component coefficient maps, check the defining relation vanishes on D_i, and extend to wedge residues with the fixed sign.
3. Compare the relative quotient to show why separate component coefficients cannot descend.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.semistableResidue.coordinate` (simp): res_i(dlog x_j)=δ_ij.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.semistableResidue.ordinary` (compatibility): res_i annihilates ordinary differentials dx_j, including dx_i=x_i dlog x_i.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.semistableResidue.relative_obstruction` (relation): res_i(Σ_j dlog x_j)=1; hence there is no induced individual residue on the relative log quotient.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.semistableResidue.node_absolute` (computation): For xy=π, absolute res_x sends dlog x to 1 and dlog y to 0.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.semistableResidue.ordinary_zero` (degenerate): An ordinary differential has zero residue.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.semistableResidue.relative_nonexample` (non-example): The proposed relative map dlog x↦1,dlog y↦0 violates dlog x+dlog y=0.

**Acceptance.**

- The map sends dlog x_i to 1 on D_i and dlog x_j to zero for j≠i.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/hk-monodromy`](#n-cr-6-hk-monodromy): Absolute component residues fix the connecting-map orientation; the relative relation obstructs individual component residues, so the triangle cannot silently use such maps.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-reduction-completion"></a>
### Log structures under reduction and completion

`CR.5/log-reduction-completion` · theorem · part CR.5

Reduction of a chart and adic completion mean pullback of its actual associated log structure along the underlying ring or scheme map. For finite semistable charts, the completed continuous log differential module is the inverse limit of the quotient modules on finite reductions and has the semistable presentation. Reduction of π retains the base generator with image zero. No statement identifies a completed complex with the derived completion of an arbitrary coefficient complex without the completion hypotheses.

**Proof outline.**

1. Pull back and logify at every finite level.
2. Use the finite free semistable presentation for continuous differentials and the imported adic/derived completion interface.

**Acceptance.**

- The nodal special fiber retains diagonal ℕ→ℕ²; completing or reducing does not replace it by a trivial log structure.

<a id="n-cr-5-cartier-type"></a>
### Morphisms of Cartier type

`CR.5/cartier-type` · definition · planet “Cartier type” · part CR.5

For an integral log morphism f:X→S in characteristic p, Cartier type means that f is integral and its relative Frobenius X→X^(p)=X×_{S,F_S}S is exact, using the fine integral log fiber product. The absolute log Frobenius is the usual Frobenius on O and multiplication by p on M. Log smoothness alone does not imply Cartier type.

**Construction.**

1. Construct absolute and relative log Frobenius with the p-power map on monoids.
2. Impose the two stated properties and verify them for the semistable diagonal chart.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsCartierType.integral` (projection): Cartier type implies the structural morphism is integral.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsCartierType.relative_frobenius_exact` (projection): The relative log Frobenius is exact.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsCartierType.base_change` (functoriality): Cartier type is stable under fine log base change.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsCartierType.semistable` (computation): The diagonal ℕ→ℕ^r in characteristic p is of Cartier type.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsCartierType.smooth_trivial` (compatibility): A smooth morphism with trivial log structures is of Cartier type.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsCartierType.root_counterexample` (non-example): For r>1 prime to p, the log smooth integral chart ℕ→ℕ, 1↦r over the log point on k[t]/t^r is not Cartier type.

**Acceptance.**

- Semistable diagonal charts are of Cartier type.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-cartier-isomorphism`](#n-cr-5-log-cartier-isomorphism): Exactness of relative log Frobenius is the hypothesis for inverse Cartier, the log Witt model and rational Frobenius isogeny; root maps give a counterexample when it fails.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-cartier-isomorphism"></a>
### Logarithmic Cartier isomorphism

`CR.5/log-cartier-isomorphism` · theorem · part CR.5

Let f:X→S be fine log smooth of Cartier type in characteristic p. Then C⁻¹:Ω^q_{X^(p)/S,log}→H^q(F_{X/S,\*}Ω^•_{X/S,log}) is an isomorphism for all q, with C⁻¹(da)=a^{p−1}da and C⁻¹(dlog m)=dlog m, interpreted under the relative Frobenius coefficient twist. It is compatible with products and base change. Exactness of relative Frobenius cannot be omitted.

**Proof outline.**

1. Reduce by log smooth charts and étale localization to the monoid-algebra complex.
2. Use relative Frobenius exactness to identify the closed-form summands with the Frobenius twist; combine the ordinary polynomial Cartier computation with logarithmic generators.

**Acceptance.**

- For a torus C⁻¹ fixes dlog t; the non-Cartier root chart fails the isomorphism.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-exactification"></a>
### Exactification of log immersions

`CR.5/log-exactification` · construction · part CR.5

For a closed immersion of fine log schemes i:X→Y (underlying closed and surjective pulled-back log map), étale locally on X factor i as X→Y^ex→Y, where the first is exact closed and the second log étale. In a chart P→Q for i, use P^ex=P^gp×_{Q^gp}Q, followed by the required local scheme base change. The exactification carries the source log structure on its closed fiber; it is only locally canonical up to the refinements used by descent.

**Construction.**

1. Construct the chart pullback P^ex and the monoid-algebra localization.
2. Use the log étale chart criterion and the closed-immersion unit adjustment; compare refinements rather than assuming a global chosen exactification.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logExactification.factor` (data): The immersion factors through an exact closed immersion followed by a log étale map.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logExactification.source_log` (compatibility): The log pullback to X agrees with its original log structure.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logExactification.refinement` (functoriality): Two local exactifications admit common log étale refinements for PD descent.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logExactification.already_exact` (degenerate): An already exact immersion can use Y itself.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logExactification.log_diagonal` (computation): For the log affine-line diagonal the exactifying neighborhood contains the unit t₂/t₁ with value 1 on X.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logExactification.ordinary_diagonal_failure` (non-example): The ordinary equation t₂−t₁ without a unit ratio does not model the logarithmic diagonal near the origin.

**Acceptance.**

- The diagonal of the logarithmic affine line acquires the unit ratio t₂/t₁.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-pd-envelope`](#n-cr-5-log-pd-envelope): An exact closed source followed by a log étale ambient map permits the ordinary PD envelope construction; common refinements give the canonical descent comparison.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-pd-envelope"></a>
### Fine log PD envelopes

`CR.5/log-pd-envelope` · construction · planet “Log PD envelopes” · part CR.5

Fix a PD base (S,L,I,γ) with fine L and O_S killed by a nonzero integer. For a closed log immersion X→Y over S, X fine and Y coherent, Kato Proposition 5.3 constructs a right adjoint to forgetting the compatible PD structure on an exact thickening. In general this adjoint may replace X by X̃. In the fixed-source specialization used here require γ to extend to Y, as in §5.5.2; then X̃≅X. Étale locally exactify, take the ordinary PD envelope supplied by CR.0, and pull back the exactifying log structure. For an exact immersion it is the ordinary PD envelope with inherited log structure.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- For the fixed-source factorization/API, the base PD structure extends to the ambient Y (Kato §5.5.2).

**Construction.**

1. Exactify and apply the generic ordinary PD envelope from CR.0.
2. Check the universal property on exact PD test thickenings and descend along étale refinements.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logPDEnvelope.factor` (constructor): Under the ambient PD-extension hypothesis, the original source X embeds exactly into its log PD envelope.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logPDEnvelope.lift` (universal-property): Every compatible exact PD thickening mapping to Y factors uniquely through the envelope.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logPDEnvelope.exact_case` (compatibility): For an exact immersion the log envelope is the ordinary PD envelope with pulled-back log structure.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logPDEnvelope.identity` (degenerate): If the base PD structure already extends to X, the envelope of X→X is X.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logPDEnvelope.log_diagonal` (computation): The log affine-line diagonal uses the divided powers of t₂/t₁−1.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logPDEnvelope.ordinary_wrong` (non-example): The ordinary PD envelope using only t₂−t₁ is not the log envelope at t=0.

**Acceptance.**

- For the log affine-line diagonal, the envelope is locally the PD polynomial ring k[t]⟨v⟩ with v=t₂/t₁−1.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-pd-stratification`](#n-cr-5-log-pd-stratification): Exactified double and triple PD diagonals supply the evaluation pullbacks and cocycle. The universal factorization also constructs products of crystalline test objects.

<a id="n-cr-5-qc-log-pd-envelope"></a>
### Quasi-coherent log PD envelopes

`CR.5/qc-log-pd-envelope` · construction · part CR.5

Let (S,M_S,I,γ) be a quasi-coherent log PD base with p^nO_S=0. For a locally closed embedding (Z,M)→(Y,N) of log S♯-schemes (so γ extends to both Z and Y) with M integral quasi-coherent and N quasi-coherent, Beilinson constructs the log PD envelope in integral quasi-coherent exact PD thickenings. Under the fine-base specialization this extends the fine envelope. Construction uses chart approximations and logarithmic coordinate thickenings. It does not prove an uncompleted envelope theorem over a base where p is not nilpotent.

**Hypotheses and conventions.**

- The source and ambient are log S♯-schemes in Beilinson §1.2: γ extends to their extended base ideals.

**Construction.**

1. Reduce étale locally to chart embeddings and finite fine approximations.
2. Construct PD polynomial coordinates and logarithmic multiplicative coordinates, quotient by the chart relations, then descend the right-adjoint universal property.
3. For p-adic bases work levelwise before taking the derived inverse limit; do not uncomplete the result.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.qcLogPDEnvelope.exact_source` (projection): The envelope has an exact PD source immersion.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.qcLogPDEnvelope.lift` (universal-property): Compatible exact integral quasi-coherent PD test thickenings have a unique factorization.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.qcLogPDEnvelope.fine_case` (compatibility): On fine charts this agrees with the fine log PD envelope.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.qcLogPDEnvelope.fine_diagonal` (compatibility): For a fine log diagonal the Beilinson and Kato envelopes coincide.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.qcLogPDEnvelope.identity` (degenerate): An identity embedding with compatible base PD structure has its identity envelope.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.qcLogPDEnvelope.uncompleted_scope` (compatibility): Over a p-nilpotent compatible base, the identity embedding of the integral quasi-coherent ℚ≥0 log point has that same log point as its envelope.

**Acceptance.**

- At each p^n level the envelope extends the fine envelope on finite charts.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

<a id="n-cr-5-log-pd-thickening"></a>
### Exact log PD thickenings

`CR.5/log-pd-thickening` · definition · part CR.5

Over a log PD base S with p^n=0, an object is an exact closed immersion U→T of integral quasi-coherent log schemes over S, with a quasi-coherent PD ideal (J,δ) defining U. Require γ to extend to T and U, and require γ and δ to extend jointly to divided powers on J+IO_T. There is no assumption IO_T⊆J. J is nil in this setting; do not require a uniform ordinary nilpotence bound absent in the source. Fine thickenings form the Kato special case.

**Construction.**

1. Use the existing DividedPowers API on affine PD ideals and descend it.
2. Impose exactness and base compatibility as the displayed mathematical conditions, with nil PD ideals in finite characteristic.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDThickening.ideal` (projection): The thickening carries its actual defining PD ideal J.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-pd-smooth"></a>
### PD smooth log thickenings

`CR.5/log-pd-smooth` · definition · part CR.5

An integral quasi-coherent log PD thickening (Z,T) over a p-nilpotent PD base is PD smooth if every map from an affine exact log PD thickening (Z′,T′) whose closed fiber maps into Z admits a lift to T as in Beilinson §1.4. Coordinate PD envelopes of polynomial/logarithmic coordinate embeddings are PD smooth, retracts are PD smooth, and envelopes in fine log smooth ambient schemes are PD smooth. Do not assert that this property is étale local; the source explicitly leaves that question open.

**Construction.**

1. Specify the affine PD lifting property over the base.
2. Lift ordinary coordinates arbitrarily and logarithmic coordinates with the unit adjustment; use the envelope universal property.
3. Use the source retract criterion and fine log smooth lifting only in their stated directions.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsPDSmooth.affine_lift` (characterisation): The affine PD test lifting property is the definition.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsPDSmooth.coordinate` (constructor): Coordinate PD thickenings are PD smooth.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsPDSmooth.retract` (structure): Retracts of PD smooth thickenings are PD smooth.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsPDSmooth.base_object` (degenerate): The base PD thickening S₀→S is PD smooth: every test thickening already has its structural map to S.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsPDSmooth.coordinate_envelope` (computation): The PD envelope of an affine coordinate embedding is PD smooth.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.IsPDSmooth.locality_caveat` (characterisation): A lift into an affine coordinate PD envelope is determined by the images of its ordinary and logarithmic coordinate generators, satisfying the base structural equations.

**Acceptance.**

- A coordinate PD envelope has the affine lifting property.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-poincare`](#n-cr-5-log-poincare): Affine lifting makes the coordinate PD resolution contractible in the Poincaré argument and lets evaluation compute crystal connections and log crystalline cohomology.
- beilinson §1.4, definition, examples and Remark: The source construction uses affine lifting makes the coordinate PD resolution contractible in the Poincaré argument and lets evaluation compute crystal connections and log crystalline cohomology.

The planned reduction is: Specify the affine PD lifting property over the base.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-crystalline-site"></a>
### Log crystalline sites

`CR.5/log-crystalline-site` · construction · planet “Log crystalline site” · part CR.5

For integral quasi-coherent Z over a p-nilpotent log PD base S♯, with the base PD structure extending to Z, objects of (Z/S)_crys are U étale over Z and exact integral quasi-coherent log PD thickenings U→T over S. Morphisms commute with source, log structure and divided powers; coverings are étale covers of T whose induced closed fibers cover U. The structure sheaf sends (U,T) to Γ(T,O_T), and the PD ideal and log sheaves are inherited from T. Fine objects recover the Kato site.

**Construction.**

1. Define the category of exact PD objects and its étale coverings.
2. Use log PD envelopes to construct products needed by the site and the morphism u:(Z/S)_crys→Z_et.
3. Verify the structure sheaf and functoriality under log PD base maps.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logCrystallineSite.structure_sections` (simp): O_crys(U,T)=Γ(T,O_T).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logCrystallineSite.pullback` (functoriality): A compatible diagram of source log schemes and log PD bases induces the crystalline pullback map.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logCrystallineSite.trivial_log` (compatibility): With trivial log structures the fine site is the ordinary crystalline site.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logCrystallineSite.identity_object` (degenerate): If Z is itself a compatible PD base object, its zero-ideal thickening is an object.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logCrystallineSite.log_diagonal_envelope` (computation): The exactified PD log diagonal is a valid site object.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.logCrystallineSite.nonexact_excluded` (non-example): An ordinary closed immersion whose log map is nonexact is excluded until exactified.

**Acceptance.**

- For trivial log structures and fine objects this specializes to the ordinary crystalline site.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-crystal`](#n-cr-5-log-crystal): Its structure sheaf and PD pullback maps define cartesian coefficient evaluations; its projection to the étale site is the functor used in log crystalline derived pushforward.
- beilinson §1.5: The source construction uses its structure sheaf and PD pullback maps define cartesian coefficient evaluations; its projection to the étale site is the functor used in log crystalline derived pushforward.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-crystal"></a>
### Logarithmic crystals

`CR.5/log-crystal` · definition · part CR.5

A log crystal is a sheaf F of O_crys-modules for which every site morphism g:(U′,T′)→(U,T) gives an isomorphism g\*F_T→F_T′ of O_T′-modules. Finite locally free, quasi-coherent and flat are additional properties of evaluations, not implicit in the word crystal. Pullback, tensor and dual on finite locally free crystals use these actual transition maps.

**Construction.**

1. Use sheaves of modules on the log crystalline site.
2. Impose the cartesian evaluation condition on every PD morphism and verify the composition coherence.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogCrystal.transition` (equivalence): Evaluation gives g\*F_T≅F_T′, coherent for identity and composition.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogCrystal.tensor` (structure): The tensor product of crystals is a crystal.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogCrystal.dual` (compatibility): For finite locally free F, evaluation of F∨ is the O_T-linear dual of F_T.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogCrystal.structure_sheaf` (computation): O_crys has its canonical cartesian transitions.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogCrystal.zero` (degenerate): The zero sheaf is a crystal.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogCrystal.arbitrary_sheaf` (non-example): A sheaf whose evaluation on a PD extension is not the base extension of its source value is not a crystal.

**Acceptance.**

- The structure sheaf is a crystal.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-pd-stratification`](#n-cr-5-log-pd-stratification): Cartesian transition isomorphisms evaluated on double/triple diagonals yield the identity and cocycle of the PD stratification; finite locally free duals remain cartesian.
- kato Definition 6.1, p.218: The source construction uses cartesian transition isomorphisms evaluated on double/triple diagonals yield the identity and cocycle of the PD stratification; finite locally free duals remain cartesian.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-pd-stratification"></a>
### Log PD stratifications

`CR.5/log-pd-stratification` · definition · part CR.5

For an embedding into a log smooth ambient scheme with log PD envelope D, a log PD stratification on an O_D-module M is an isomorphism ε:p₂\*M→p₁\*M on the log PD diagonal D(1), identity on the diagonal and satisfying p₁₂\*ε∘p₂₃\*ε=p₁₃\*ε on D(2). The diagonal is log exactified before PD enveloping. Its first PD infinitesimal term gives a log connection.

**Construction.**

1. Evaluate a crystal on the two PD projections.
2. Use the cartesian condition and the triple diagonal to construct ε and its cocycle, with identity on the diagonal.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDStratification.diagonal` (simp): Diagonal pullback of ε is the identity.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDStratification.cocycle` (relation): The triple diagonal satisfies the stated cocycle.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDStratification.first_order` (compatibility): The first infinitesimal difference of ε is a Leibniz log connection.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDStratification.structure` (computation): The structure crystal has the canonical multiplication-compatible stratification.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDStratification.zero` (degenerate): The zero module has its unique stratification.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogPDStratification.missing_cocycle` (non-example): An isomorphism on the double diagonal without the triple cocycle is not a PD stratification.

**Acceptance.**

- The structure crystal gives the identity coefficient stratification.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/crystal-connection-equivalence`](#n-cr-5-crystal-connection-equivalence): Differentiating the first PD order gives the connection; diagonal identity and triple cocycle supply its Leibniz rule and zero curvature. Taylor coefficients recover the stratification.
- kato Proposition 6.5 and proof §6.6–6.7, pp.219–220: The source construction uses differentiating the first PD order gives the connection; diagonal identity and triple cocycle supply its Leibniz rule and zero curvature. Taylor coefficients recover the stratification.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-connection"></a>
### Integrable logarithmic connections

`CR.5/log-connection` · definition · part CR.5

A log connection on an O_D-module M over a log smooth ambient Y/S is an additive map ∇:M→M⊗_O_D Ω¹_{Y/S,log}|_D satisfying ∇(am)=a∇m+m⊗da. Integrability means the degree-two curvature vanishes in the coefficient log de Rham complex. Morphisms are horizontal O_D-linear maps. On formal evaluations use p-adically complete modules and continuous connections.

**Construction.**

1. Use the universal log differential module in the Leibniz rule.
2. Extend ∇ to the graded complex; identify ∇² with the explicit curvature map.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogConnection.leibniz` (relation): ∇(am)=a∇m+m⊗da.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogConnection.curvature` (characterisation): Integrability is vanishing of the degree-two composite.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogConnection.horizontal` (functoriality): A horizontal linear map induces a map of coefficient log complexes.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogConnection.structure` (computation): The connection on O_D is ordinary d valued in log forms.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogConnection.zero` (degenerate): The zero module has the zero integrable connection.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogConnection.nonintegrable` (non-example): On a two-variable smooth chart, the rank-one connection d+x dy has curvature dx∧dy and is not integrable.

**Acceptance.**

- The structure module has connection d.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/log-pd-de-rham`](#n-cr-5-log-pd-de-rham): Its Leibniz map gives the coefficient differential, zero curvature makes its square vanish, and horizontal maps give maps of coefficient complexes and relative Gauss–Manin coefficients.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-quasi-nilpotence"></a>
### Logarithmic quasi-nilpotence

`CR.5/log-quasi-nilpotence` · definition · part CR.5

Choose a local basis dlog t_i for log differentials and write ∇_i for its coefficient operators. Log quasi-nilpotence means that for every local m, products over i of the falling factorial operators ∏_{j=0}^{a_i−1}(∇_i−j) vanish for every multiindex a with sufficiently large total degree |a| in finite-level evaluations; formally they tend to zero in the p-adic topology. The condition is independent of such a log basis. On ordinary invertible coordinates it agrees with the usual PD Taylor quasi-nilpotence; plain powers ∇_i^{a_i} are not the log criterion.

**Construction.**

1. Express logarithmic PD Taylor coefficients in unit ratios u_i−1.
2. Their coefficients are falling factorials of logarithmic operators; use PD diagonal coordinate changes to show independence.
3. At formal level require convergence modulo every p^n.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogQuasiNilpotent.falling_factorial` (characterisation): The local condition is eventual vanishing of the displayed falling factorial operators.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogQuasiNilpotent.coordinate_independent` (compatibility): Equivalent logarithmic coordinate bases give the same property.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogQuasiNilpotent.formal_mod_pn` (characterisation): Formal quasi-nilpotence is the finite-level condition modulo each p^n.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogQuasiNilpotent.zero_residue` (degenerate): The constant zero logarithmic operator is quasi-nilpotent.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogQuasiNilpotent.integer_residue` (computation): A scalar operator λ=1 has ∇(∇−1)=0, though its positive powers are not zero in characteristic zero.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.LogQuasiNilpotent.nonintegral_residue` (non-example): For a rank-one logarithmic operator with residue λ not in ℤ_p, the falling factorials need not converge p-adically; for p=2, λ=1/2 fails.

**Acceptance.**

- For a constant residue λ∈ℤ≥0, the falling factorial vanishes once the index exceeds λ.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.5/crystal-connection-equivalence`](#n-cr-5-crystal-connection-equivalence): Falling factorial convergence makes the logarithmic PD Taylor sum defined and supplies its inverse to evaluation, including residue 1 which ordinary operator powers would reject.
- kato Theorem 6.2(b)(iii), Remark 6.3: The source construction uses falling factorial convergence makes the logarithmic PD Taylor sum defined and supplies its inverse to evaluation, including residue 1 which ordinary operator powers would reject.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`CR.5/log-connection`](#n-cr-5-log-connection), [`CR.5/log-pd-stratification`](#n-cr-5-log-pd-stratification).

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`CR.5/crystal-connection-equivalence`](#n-cr-5-crystal-connection-equivalence).

- [hk](#src-hk), §2.17, log PD Taylor coefficients: “log” — The logarithmic operators use falling factorials instead of ordinary powers.

The one-coordinate falling-factorial slice/tests are meaningful. coordinate_independent is merely conjugacy of one operator; formal_mod_pn is one-way descent to an arbitrary quotient. Neither gives the stated log-coordinate-change or formal iff on all p-power levels.

<a id="n-cr-5-crystal-connection-equivalence"></a>
### Crystals and log connections

`CR.5/crystal-connection-equivalence` · theorem · part CR.5

For a fine closed log embedding X→Y with Y log smooth over a p-nilpotent fine log PD base S, evaluation on the log PD envelope D gives an equivalence between crystals on X/S and O_D-modules with integrable log quasi-nilpotent connection valued in Ω¹_{Y/S,log}|_D. The coordinate PD-smooth integral quasi-coherent extension uses Beilinson §1.7 and its PD smooth hypotheses. Finite locally free evaluations correspond to finite locally free modules. Formal versions use compatible levels and p-adically complete modules.

**Proof outline.**

1. Differentiate the PD diagonal stratification to obtain the integrable connection.
2. Recover the stratification from the convergent logarithmic Taylor series, using falling factorials and PD unit-ratio coordinates.
3. Descend the cartesian evaluation data to the site; apply Beilinson finite-chart approximation for its coordinate PD-smooth extension.

**Acceptance.**

- The structure crystal corresponds to d; logarithmic residue 1 uses the binomial Taylor factor, not the exponential of ordinary powers.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-pd-de-rham"></a>
### Filtered logarithmic PD de Rham complexes

`CR.5/log-pd-de-rham` · construction · part CR.5

For a log PD envelope D in a log smooth ambient Y/S, form M⊗_O_D Ω^•_{Y/S,log}|_D with the coefficient connection differential, imposing dγ_n(x)=γ_{n−1}(x)dx for the PD ideal. Its PD filtration on the structure complex is F^mΩ^a=J^[m−a]Ω^a, with J^[b]=O for b≤0. For filtered coefficients use the convolution filtration and require Griffiths transversality. This uses the generic PD filtration owned by CR.0.

**Construction.**

1. Use the coefficient log complex on the envelope and impose the PD differential identity.
2. Import the PD ideal filtration and form its degree-shifted filtration; prove d preserves it using the identity for γ.

<a id="n-cr-5-log-poincare"></a>
### Log PD Poincaré lemma

`CR.5/log-poincare` · theorem · planet “Log PD Poincaré lemma” · part CR.5

Under the fine log smooth embedding hypotheses of the crystal–connection equivalence, Ru_\*F is naturally represented by the log PD de Rham complex of F_D. For a coordinate PD-smooth integral quasi-coherent embedding, Beilinson gives the analogous comparison, including the compatible PD filtration. The map is induced by the crystal evaluation and linearized log PD resolution; the claim is not an ordinary de Rham comparison for an arbitrary singular ambient scheme.

**Proof outline.**

1. Resolve the crystal by the linearized PD diagonal complex.
2. In ordinary/logarithmic coordinates contract the PD additive and multiplicative coordinate directions.
3. Push forward and compare evaluation; use the PD Taylor equivalence and compatible filtrations.

**Acceptance.**

- The log affine-line resolution uses divided powers of the unit-ratio difference.

<a id="n-cr-5-embedding-descent"></a>
### Logarithmic embedding-system descent

`CR.5/embedding-descent` · theorem · part CR.5

Choose an étale hypercover X_•→X and compatible embeddings into log smooth ambient schemes, or coordinate PD-smooth integral quasi-coherent thickenings. The total derived pushforward of the cosimplicial log PD de Rham complexes represents Ru_\*F and is independent of the embeddings by common refinements. At finite levels these complexes are bounded below uniformly, so use bounded-below hypercover descent; no repleteness of the ordinary étale topos is assumed.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use local log smooth/coordinate PD embeddings to build the hypercover system.
2. Apply the local Poincaré lemma termwise and bounded-below hypercover descent.
3. Compare two systems on their common refinement and use the resulting canonical derived isomorphisms.

**Acceptance.**

- Changing a semistable chart leaves the computed log crystalline complex canonically equivalent.

`CR.5/p-adic-log-crystalline` · construction · part CR.5

For compatible log PD bases S_n with p^n=0 and compatible coefficient crystals F_n on X/S_n, define RΓ_logcrys(X/S,F)=Rlim_n RΓ(X/S_n,F_n). <a id="n-cr-5-unique-p-divisible-lift"></a>
### Unique lifting of p-divisible log structures

`CR.5/unique-p-divisible-lift` · theorem · part CR.5

Let (Z,M) be integral quasi-coherent over F_p and suppose the sharp sheaf M/O_Z× is uniquely p-divisible. For an ordinary compatible PD thickening Z→T over a p^n-nilpotent PD base, M lifts uniquely to a log structure on T making the immersion exact. The lifted log structure is functorial in PD thickenings and compatible with Frobenius. Thus ordinary and log crystalline sites agree after this canonical lift. Arbitrary integral quasi-coherent or fine log structures do not have this uniqueness assertion.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use unique p^n-division in the characteristic sheaf to select roots of log sections.
2. Raise arbitrary lifts to suitable p-powers; PD nilpotence makes the result independent of the choices, and glue.
3. Recover the unique compatible log sheaf on every PD thickening and compare the two sites.

**Acceptance.**

- The rational characteristic log point satisfies the hypothesis; the characteristic ℕ of the standard fine log point does not.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`CR.5:log-algebra/qc-log-scheme`](#n-cr-5-log-algebra-qc-log-scheme), [`CR.5:log-algebra/characteristic-monoid`](#n-cr-5-log-algebra-characteristic-monoid), [`CR.5/log-pd-thickening`](#n-cr-5-log-pd-thickening), [`CR.5/log-crystalline-site`](#n-cr-5-log-crystalline-site).

<a id="layer-cr-6"></a>
## CR.6 — Hyodo–Kato complexes and semistable structure

*Coverage in the CR.5 part: planned. 27 nodes, 5 planets.*

The layer plans Hyodo–Kato theory for semistable reduction and its analytic continuations used by the papers routed here.

- **The complex and its operators.** The log Witt base (ℕ → W(k), 1 ↦ 0); integral and rational Hyodo–Kato complexes of the special log fibre; Frobenius; monodromy N as the connecting map of the right-wedge θ triangle, with Nφ = pφN; finiteness, the Frobenius isogeny and the nilpotence of N; the comparison with the log de Rham–Witt complex of Hyodo–Kato §4.19.
- **The comparison with de Rham cohomology.** The normalised unit logarithm; the uniformizer-dependent map ρ_π after the K₀ → K scalar extension, the Hyodo–Kato comparison theorem, and the change-of-uniformizer formula ρ_{πu} = ρ_π∘exp(log_K(u)N); products; good reduction (N = 0) and the Tate curve (N ≠ 0, N² = 0); Qian's one-parameter families; ramified base change with normalised monodromy.
- **Convergent and analytic versions.** The convergent log complexes of an embedding system, analytic proper support on tubes, the convergent monodromy triangle, the comparison with the log Witt models of CR.4 and Sato's residue variant (Disegni–Liu, Appendix B); the comparison with log rigid Hyodo–Kato cohomology (Grosse-Klönne); Stein curves and semistable curve towers with completed tensor products (Colmez–Dospinescu–Nizioł). The tubes, rigid complexes and Fréchet topologies are imported from PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.4, or from the Part II that structural proposal S15 asks for.

CohomologyComparisons CP.4 assembles these with B_st and the étale comparison. The five planets are the Hyodo–Kato complex, monodromy, the Frobenius–monodromy relation, the Hyodo–Kato map and the comparison theorem.

**Still open in this layer.**

- Provide CR.4 log Witt and Sato residue objects and the RD Part II analytic/topological interfaces.
- Supply the Tate-curve geometric monodromy calculation and compare its basis orientation.
- Restrict HK operator/comparison statements to actual geometric constructions and coherent scalar extensions; restore derived product/good-reduction/Tate tests and complete analytic coefficient topology.

`CR.6/log-witt-base` · construction · part CR.5

<a id="n-cr-6-integral-hk"></a>
### Integral Hyodo–Kato complexes

`CR.6/integral-hk` · construction · planet “Hyodo–Kato complex” · part CR.5

Let O_K be a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue k, and X a proper semistable model with special log fiber Y over k^log. Define C_HK,ℤ(Y)=Rlim_n RΓ_logcrys(Y/W_n(k)^log,O), with the canonical PD ideal (p). The construction uses the actual reduced diagonal semistable log structure. Finite-level embedding descent is integral; the cohomology can have p-torsion.

**Construction.**

1. Apply the completed log crystalline construction to the standard Witt log base.
2. Choose compatible embeddings/hypercovers and their integral PD log complexes; retain derived inverse limits.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.integralHK.finite_level` (projection): There are coherent maps to RΓ_logcrys(Y/W_n(k)^log).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.integralHK.embedding_model` (compatibility): A compatible log PD embedding system computes the same integral complex.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.integralHK.pullback` (functoriality): A map of proper semistable models induces a contravariant map of integral HK complexes.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.integralHK.point` (computation): The relative log point has integral HK=W(k) in degree zero.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.integralHK.zero_cohomology` (degenerate): Its positive-degree cohomology vanishes.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.integralHK.torsion_retained` (non-example): Integral HK is not defined by first killing p-torsion.

**Acceptance.**

- For Y the log point over itself, C_HK,ℤ=W(k).

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/rational-hk`](#n-cr-6-rational-hk): Its derived inverse limit retains torsion and is rationalized explicitly. Its coherent restriction and embedding maps carry Frobenius and the monodromy boundary through that step.
- hk §3.1–3.3, pp.242–244: The source construction uses its derived inverse limit retains torsion and is rationalized explicitly. Its coherent restriction and embedding maps carry Frobenius and the monodromy boundary through that step.

<a id="n-cr-6-rational-hk"></a>
### Rational Hyodo–Kato complexes

`CR.6/rational-hk` · construction · part CR.5

With the same proper semistable hypotheses let K₀=Frac W(k)=W(k)[1/p] and C_HK(Y)=C_HK,ℤ(Y)⊗^L_{W(k)}K₀. Its cohomology D^m is finite dimensional over K₀, with the Frobenius and monodromy constructed below. Rationalization is an explicit scalar extension and does not identify integral cohomology lattices with torsion-free ones.

**Construction.**

1. Invert p by the derived scalar extension, which is flat.
2. Transport the finite-level operators and their coherent identities to the rational complex.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.rationalHK.cohomology` (compatibility): Rational cohomology is integral cohomology tensored with K₀.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.rationalHK.map` (functoriality): Pullback maps commute with rationalization.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.rationalHK.torsion_killed` (simp): Every p-power torsion class maps to zero.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.rationalHK.point` (computation): For the relative log point the rational complex is K₀ in degree zero.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.rationalHK.p_torsion` (degenerate): A p-power torsion cohomology summand vanishes after rationalization.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.rationalHK.integral_not_iso` (non-example): The scalar-extension map is not asserted to preserve a p-torsion integral lattice.

**Acceptance.**

- H^m(C_HK)=H^m(C_HK,ℤ)[1/p].

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/hk-comparison-map`](#n-cr-6-hk-comparison-map): Explicit K₀ scalar extension gives the domain of ρ_π; finite-dimensional cohomology and Frobenius isogeny make the nilpotence and uniformizer exponential arguments applicable.
- hk §3.2, p.243; Theorem 5.1, pp.262–263: The source construction uses explicit K₀ scalar extension gives the domain of ρ_π; finite-dimensional cohomology and Frobenius isogeny make the nilpotence and uniformizer exponential arguments applicable.

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-frobenius"></a>
### Hyodo–Kato Frobenius

`CR.6/hk-frobenius` · construction · part CR.5

Absolute Frobenius of the special log fiber, together with Witt Frobenius σ and multiplication by p on the base chart, gives a σ-semilinear chain endomorphism φ of integral HK, hence of rational HK. Equivalently its linearization is σ\*C_HK→C_HK. On a lifted coordinate de Rham model φ in degree q is p^q times the coefficient Frobenius on logarithmic q-forms, with Frobenius-lift comparisons supplied by descent.

**Construction.**

1. Use the absolute log Frobenius and the base σ to induce the crystalline map.
2. Compute φ(dlog x)=p dlog x on a coordinate lift, then descend the model-independent endomorphism.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkFrobenius.semilinear` (relation): φ(ax)=σ(a)φ(x).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkFrobenius.linearization` (compatibility): The associated σ-twisted linear map is the linearization, not an ordinary K₀-linear φ.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkFrobenius.forms` (simp): On q-fold logarithmic generators the Frobenius multiplier is p^q.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkFrobenius.point` (computation): On W(k) in degree zero, φ=σ.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkFrobenius.log_one_form` (computation): A logarithmic one-form acquires the factor p.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkFrobenius.not_linear` (non-example): For k=F_{p²} and a∈k with a^p≠a, on degree-zero W(k) the Teichmüller element satisfies φ([a])=[a^p]≠[a]φ(1).

**Acceptance.**

- On H⁰ of the log point φ is σ.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/n-phi-relation`](#n-cr-6-n-phi-relation): The degree-one multiplier p on dlog t makes the triangle commute up to p, giving Nφ=pφN. Semilinearity and its invertible rational linearization are used in the nilpotence proof.
- hk §3.2–3.4: The source construction uses the degree-one multiplier p on dlog t makes the triangle commute up to p, giving Nφ=pφN. Semilinearity and its invertible rational linearization are used in the nilpotence proof.

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-monodromy"></a>
### Hyodo–Kato monodromy

`CR.6/hk-monodromy` · construction · planet “Monodromy operator” · part CR.5

Embed the special log fiber over the log parameter base W_n(k)[t]^log, then use its PD t-envelope and specialize t=0 in the derived category. Let C be the relative log complex and C̃ the complex relative to the trivial Witt log structure. With θ=dlog t and right wedge by θ, 0→C[−1]→C̃→C→0 defines the connecting endomorphism N:C→C. The equivalent PD logarithmic diagonal Taylor description takes the first coefficient of the unit-ratio parameter. Fix this convention throughout.

**Construction.**

1. Use the embedding system over W_n[t]^log and form absolute and relative PD log complexes.
2. Take the connecting map of the right-wedge θ short exact sequence after derived t=0 specialization.
3. Identify it with the first logarithmic PD Taylor coefficient and pass through Rlim and rationalization.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkMonodromy.boundary` (characterisation): N is the connecting morphism of the fixed right-wedge θ triangle.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkMonodromy.linear` (structure): N is W(k)-linear integrally and K₀-linear rationally.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkMonodromy.embedding_independence` (compatibility): Common embedding refinements preserve the connecting endomorphism.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkMonodromy.point` (degenerate): For the relative log point N=0.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkMonodromy.tate_block` (computation): On a normalized Tate block, N(e₁)=e₀ and N(e₀)=0.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkMonodromy.wedge_sign` (computation): On the normalized Tate block, reversing the connecting-map sign gives N′(e₁)=−e₀, whereas the fixed convention gives N(e₁)=e₀.

**Acceptance.**

- N vanishes on the relative log point and is compatible with base change.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/uniformizer-change`](#n-cr-6-uniformizer-change): The first unit-ratio Taylor coefficient is N, so its higher coefficients yield the finite positive-sign exponential. The absolute-relative triangle also compares it with the log Witt and convergent models.
- hk §3.5–3.6, pp.244–246; §4.20: The source construction uses the first unit-ratio Taylor coefficient is N, so its higher coefficients yield the finite positive-sign exponential. The absolute-relative triangle also compares it with the log Witt and convergent models.

<a id="n-cr-6-n-phi-relation"></a>
### Frobenius–monodromy relation

`CR.6/n-phi-relation` · theorem · planet “Frobenius–monodromy relation” · part CR.5

For the HK operators in the right-wedge convention, Nφ=pφN as semilinear maps on the rational complex and on finite-level/coherent integral models wherever defined. Equivalently N∘φ_lin=p φ_lin∘σ\*N. The factor comes from Frobenius(θ)=pθ in the defining triangle.

**Proof outline.**

1. Apply Frobenius to the absolute-relative short exact sequence.
2. The left wedge map scales by p since θ does; functoriality of the boundary gives Nφ=pφN.

**Acceptance.**

- For φ(e₀)=e₀, φ(e₁)=pe₁, N(e₁)=e₀ both sides on e₁ equal pe₀.

The planned reduction is: Apply Frobenius to the absolute-relative short exact sequence.

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-finiteness"></a>
### Finiteness and Frobenius isogeny

`CR.6/hk-finiteness` · theorem · part CR.5

For a proper fine log smooth integral Y/k^log of Cartier type, finite-level log crystalline cohomology has finite W_n(k)-length and the completed cohomology is a finite W(k)-module. After inverting p, φ_lin is an isomorphism. Semistable special log fibers satisfy these hypotheses. Integral Frobenius is only an isogeny; it need not be invertible before rationalization.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use log smooth integral embeddings and proper coherent cohomology to obtain finite-level length and completed finiteness.
2. Use the Cartier comparison and bounded differential rank to construct Frobenius inverses up to a bounded power of p on the pro-system.
3. Invert p to obtain the linearized isomorphism.

**Acceptance.**

- For a good reduction curve this recovers the ordinary crystalline finiteness and Frobenius isogeny.

The planned reduction is: Use log smooth integral embeddings and proper coherent cohomology to obtain finite-level length and completed finiteness.

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-nilpotence"></a>
### Nilpotence of Hyodo–Kato monodromy

`CR.6/hk-nilpotence` · theorem · part CR.5

On each finite-dimensional rational HK cohomology D^m, N is nilpotent. More generally, for finite-dimensional K₀-space D, σ-semilinear invertible φ, K₀-linear N and Nφ=pφN, with σ preserving the p-adic valuation, N^dim(D)=0. No such conclusion is asserted for arbitrary infinite-dimensional modules or noninvertible Frobenius.

**Proof outline.**

1. Compare characteristic-polynomial coefficients of N under the σ-semilinear conjugation and p-scaling.
2. A coefficient of positive degree must have its valuation shifted by a nonzero multiple of v(p), while σ preserves valuation; hence it vanishes.
3. Apply Cayley–Hamilton to the polynomial T^dim(D).

**Acceptance.**

- A two-dimensional Tate block has N²=0 and N≠0; a zero Frobenius cannot be used to deduce nilpotence.

**Depends on.** this roadmap: [`CR.6/hk-finiteness`](#n-cr-6-hk-finiteness), [`CR.6/n-phi-relation`](#n-cr-6-n-phi-relation).

**Used by in this roadmap.** [`CR.6/uniformizer-change`](#n-cr-6-uniformizer-change).

**Proposed location.** `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/LogCrystalline`, namespace `TauCeti.LogCrystalline`; declaration `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hk_monodromy_nilpotent`.

**Suggested file.** declaration named in the code.

**Sources.**

- [hk](#src-hk), §3.2, p.243; algebraic deduction from §3.4, p.244: “nilpotent” — The passage is used for On each finite-dimensional rational HK cohomology D^m, N is nilpotent. The planned reduction is: Compare characteristic-polynomial coefficients of N under the σ-semilinear conjugation and p-scaling.

**Review.** REV-CrystallineCohomology--CR.5: corrected. Corrected source page to 243. The abstract finite-dimensional nilpotence deduction has invertible semilinear φ and valuation-preserving σ with 0\<|p|\<1; these rule out the false infinite-dimensional/noninvertible cases.

### Log de Rham–Witt model

`CR.6/log-de-rham-witt-model` · comparison · part CR.5

Import the log de Rham–Witt complex W_nω_Y from CR.4 for fine log smooth Cartier-type Y/k^log. HK §4.19 gives W_nω_Y≃Ru_\*O_{Y/W_n(k)^log}, compatible with Frobenius and restriction in n. In the semistable case its absolute-relative log Witt sequence gives the same N as the embedding-system triangle (§4.20). Take Rlim integrally and invert p only at the stated rational step.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use the CR.4 logarithmic Witt complex and its operators as the supplied object.
2. Map the log PD embedding complex to the Witt complex via the Witt PD thickening and universal log differentials.
3. Identify the absolute-relative triangles on embedding systems and pass to compatible levels.

**Acceptance.**

- The comparison fixes dlog generators and preserves N and the Frobenius factor p in degree one.

<a id="n-cr-6-unit-logarithm"></a>
### Normalized logarithms of units

`CR.6/unit-logarithm` · construction · part CR.5

For the complete mixed-characteristic DVR O_K with perfect k and the fixed W(k) coefficient map, write u=[ū](1+a), a∈m_K. Define log_K(u)=Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n+1}a^n/n, using the convergent p-adic series. It kills Teichmüller units and torsion units and is additive under multiplication. Only units are needed for uniformizer changes; no value log(π) is prescribed by this definition.

**Construction.**

1. Divide the unit by its Teichmüller lift to obtain a principal unit.
2. Use convergence of the usual p-adic logarithm series and multiplicativity on principal units, including torsion; extend by zero on Teichmüller units.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.unitLog.mul` (relation): log_K(uv)=log_K(u)+log_K(v).
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.unitLog.teichmuller` (simp): log_K([a])=0 for a∈k×.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.unitLog.principal_series` (characterisation): On 1+m_K the value is the displayed convergent series.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.unitLog.one` (degenerate): log_K(1)=0.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.unitLog.torsion` (computation): For a torsion unit ζ, log_K(ζ)=0.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.unitLog.branch_warning` (characterisation): For c≠0 the additive homomorphisms ℓ and ℓ+c·v_K on K× agree on O_K× and differ on π by c. Thus the unit normalization alone does not determine a value on π.

**Acceptance.**

- log_K(uv)=log_K(u)+log_K(v).

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/uniformizer-change`](#n-cr-6-uniformizer-change): The normalized logarithm of the unit π′/π is the scalar in exp(log(u)N); killing Teichmüller and torsion units specifies this scalar without assigning any log(π).
- hk Proof §5.5, pp.265–266: The source construction uses the normalized logarithm of the unit π′/π is the scalar in exp(log(u)N); killing Teichmüller and torsion units specifies this scalar without assigning any log(π).

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-comparison-map"></a>
### Uniformizer-dependent Hyodo–Kato maps

`CR.6/hk-comparison-map` · construction · planet “Hyodo–Kato map” · part CR.5

For proper semistable X/O_K, K₀=Frac W(k) and chosen uniformizer π, construct ρ_π:C_HK(Y)⊗^L_{K₀}K→RΓ(X_K,Ω^•_{X_K/K,log}). For the usual semistable model with only vertical boundary, generic log structure is trivial and the target is ordinary de Rham. The map uses the PD parameter envelope t↦π and a rational Frobenius iteration to compare t=0 and t=π; it is not defined as an integral comparison or a choice-free map.

**Construction.**

1. Use the PD envelope of the uniformizer relation in W_n[t]^log and its two base specializations.
2. Iterate Frobenius enough to move the maximal ideal into p times the parameter algebra; compare by Frobenius isogeny and log crystalline base change.
3. Pass to the rational inverse-limit comparison and proper formal functions for the generic log de Rham target.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkComparisonMap.pullback` (functoriality): ρ_π is natural for morphisms of the proper semistable models.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkComparisonMap.rational_domain` (data): Its domain is the explicitly rationalized HK complex extended from K₀ to K.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkComparisonMap.generic_log` (compatibility): For vertical semistable boundary its target is ordinary generic-fiber de Rham.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkComparisonMap.point` (computation): For the base point the map is the canonical K₀⊗K→K identification.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkComparisonMap.good_reduction` (degenerate): When N=0 the unit-change transformation of ρ is the identity.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.hkComparisonMap.integral_warning` (non-example): Already on the base point, the rational domain contains p⁻¹∈K₀ while the integral degree-zero HK lattice W(k) does not contain p⁻¹.

**Acceptance.**

- Good reduction specializes to the crystalline–de Rham map independent of the uniformizer.

### Hyodo–Kato comparison theorem

`CR.6/hk-comparison` · theorem · planet “Hyodo–Kato comparison theorem” · part CR.5

For a proper semistable X over a complete mixed-characteristic DVR with perfect residue k, the map ρ_π is a quasi-isomorphism after the displayed K₀→K scalar extension. On every degree, H^m_HK(Y)⊗_{K₀}K≅H^m_dR(X_K). For the more general proper fine log smooth integral Cartier-type model of HK Theorem 5.1 use the log de Rham generic fiber. CP.4 owns assembly with B_st and the étale comparison.

**Proof outline.**

1. Apply the rational Frobenius-isogeny comparison on the PD parameter envelope.
2. Use radicial log crystalline base change under HK §2.23 hypotheses and proper formal functions.
3. Identify the completed generic-fiber complex with algebraic log de Rham and conclude the constructed map is an isomorphism.

**Acceptance.**

- The point and good reduction comparisons coincide with their ordinary crystalline counterparts.

<a id="n-cr-6-uniformizer-change"></a>
### Change of uniformizer

`CR.6/uniformizer-change` · theorem · part CR.5

For π′=πu with u∈O_K×, in the fixed right-wedge monodromy convention and normalized unit logarithm, ρ_{πu}=ρ_π∘exp(log_K(u)N). On H^m the exponential is the finite sum Σ_{j=0}^{s−1}(log_K(u)N)^j/j! for N^s=0. The plus sign is derived from the unit-ratio logarithmic PD Taylor expansion. Different sign conventions for N require the corresponding changed formula.

**Proof outline.**

1. Compare the two parameter maps t↦π and t↦πu using the log diagonal unit ratio.
2. Its divided-power Taylor expansion has coefficients N^j/j! and argument +log(u).
3. Use nilpotence to truncate and check the two unit changes compose by additivity of log and multiplication of commuting exponentials.

**Acceptance.**

- On N(e₁)=e₀, N(e₀)=0, the transformation sends e₁ to e₁+log(u)e₀; successive unit changes agree with multiplication of units.

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-products"></a>
### Products and Hyodo–Kato comparison

`CR.6/hk-products` · theorem · part CR.5

For proper fine log smooth integral Cartier-type models for which the log fiber product stays in those hypotheses, rational HK has the Künneth quasi-isomorphism C_HK(Y₁)⊗^L C_HK(Y₂)→C_HK(Y₁×^logY₂). The operators are φ₁⊗φ₂ and N₁⊗1+1⊗N₂, and ρ_π respects the de Rham product comparison. The ordinary product of two strictly semistable models need not itself be strictly semistable; use the stated log product or an allowed semistable refinement.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use the ordinary derived cup-product/Künneth machinery owned by CR.3 and the enhanced tensor from E1. Adapt the PD de Rham resolutions and descent to the fine smooth integral logarithmic product, as in Kato’s final Künneth theorem on p.222; retain its quasi-compact/quasi-separated and flat-crystal hypotheses before proper rational scalar extension.
2. Tensor the absolute-relative triangles to identify N as the sum of factor operators.
3. Use the naturality of the PD parameter comparison for the common uniformizer and tensor the nilpotent exponentials.

**Acceptance.**

- Two Tate blocks satisfy Nφ=pφN on their tensor product, and the uniformizer-change exponential factors as the tensor of the factor exponentials.

<a id="n-cr-6-hk-good-reduction"></a>
### Good reduction monodromy

`CR.6/hk-good-reduction` · theorem · part CR.5

If X/O_K is proper smooth with the log structure pulled back from the base valuation chart, then its HK complex is ordinary crystalline cohomology of X_k, N=0, and ρ_π is the ordinary crystalline–de Rham comparison. Therefore changing the uniformizer by a unit has no effect.

**Proof outline.**

1. Strictness removes the relative log generators and identifies the log site with the ordinary one.
2. The absolute-relative parameter triangle splits, so its boundary N vanishes.
3. Compare the PD construction with the ordinary crystalline–de Rham map.

**Acceptance.**

- For a proper smooth elliptic curve with good reduction, N=0 in H¹.

For a split Tate elliptic curve E_q/K with v_K(q)=n>0 and a proper semistable model, rational H¹_HK has a slope basis e₀,e₁ with φ(e₀)=e₀, φ(e₁)=pe₁ and N(e₀)=0, N(e₁)=n e₀, in the fixed orientation. Thus N≠0, N²=0 and Nφ=pφN. Rescaling e₀ by the nonzero rational factor n gives the normalized block N(e₁)=e₀; specify the basis rescaling rather than claiming the integral lattice has unit monodromy.

3. Compare this residue boundary with the fixed HK triangle, then compute the displayed matrices. The complete source derivation is tracked as a gap until its Tate-curve locator is supplied.

<a id="n-cr-6-qian-family-model"></a>
### Proper one-parameter logarithmic comparison

`CR.6/qian-family-model` · comparison · part CR.5

Let Y be a proper fine log smooth family over a neighborhood of T=0 in W(k)[T]^log, with chart ℕ, 1↦T. Write Y₀ for its T=0 log fiber, Y_n for reduction modulo p^n, and Ȳ_n for the fiber over W_n(k)^log. The finite-level PD Poincaré comparison identifies RΓ_logcrys(Ȳ₁/W_n^log) with the relative log de Rham complex of Ȳ_n, compatibly with the boundary N from the absolute-relative dlog T sequence. The compatible inverse-limit and rational cohomology comparison uses proper finite W-cohomology, not log smoothness alone.

**Proof outline.**

1. Use the finite-level log smooth lift and PD Poincaré lemma, comparing the right-wedge dlog T sequences to prove N compatibility.
2. Use the universal-coefficient short exact sequence 0→H^i/p^n→H^i_n→H^{i+1}[p^n]→0, whose last transitions multiply by p.
3. Proper finite W-modules kill the inverse limit of the torsion terms and identify completed cohomology, then rationalize.

**Acceptance.**

- The comparison is N-equivariant and commutes with W_{n+1}→W_n; it does not use Dwork-specific geometry.

<a id="n-cr-6-convergent-log-complex"></a>
### Convergent logarithmic embedding complexes

`CR.6/convergent-log-complex` · construction · part CR.5

For a fine finite-type log scheme X over k^log, take the embedding system of DL Appendix B.1 into log smooth W[t]^log schemes, completed on the special fiber. Using the analytic tube and specialization functors supplied by RD.4, define ω_X=Ru_\*Rs_\*Ω_{lift/W^log} on the tube and its absolute variant ω̃_X using Ω_{lift/W}. These are rational convergent logarithmic complexes in this source. They are not defined as the classical log crystalline complex or as an overconvergent j† complex by renaming.

**Construction.**

1. Import the analytic tube, quasi-étale site, specialization and embedding independence interface from the analytic owner.
2. Apply its de Rham complex to the relative and absolute log forms of the fixed embedding system.
3. Use common refinements to make the resulting specialized complexes independent of the embedding.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.convergentLogComplex.relative` (projection): The relative complex uses the W^log differential quotient.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.convergentLogComplex.absolute` (projection): The absolute variant uses the trivial-log Witt base and retains dlog t.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.convergentLogComplex.refinement` (functoriality): Common embedding refinements induce canonical quasi-isomorphisms.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.convergentLogComplex.point` (computation): For a point relative to its log base, ω has K₀ only in degree zero.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.convergentLogComplex.identity_refinement` (degenerate): An identity embedding refinement induces the identity comparison.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.convergentLogComplex.not_overconvergent_by_name` (computation): For the log base point the absolute complex retains K₀·dlog(t) in degree one; the relative complex kills that generator and has no positive-degree cohomology.

**Acceptance.**

- For a strict semistable special fiber the resulting complexes admit the stated rational log Witt comparison.

<a id="n-cr-6-tube-proper-support"></a>
### Proper support on open analytic tubes

`CR.6/tube-proper-support` · construction · part CR.5

For an open U⊂X in the DL embedding setting, let g:]X∖U[→]X[ be the open analytic tube inclusion. On the source quasi-étale tube site define f_!F=ker(F→g_\*g\*F), with the exactness properties in DL Definition B.1. Apply Ru_\*Rs_\* to the supported de Rham complex to define ω_(U,X) and ω̃_(U,X). This is analytic-tube support. There is a natural map from special-fiber F_!F\*Rs_\* to Rs_\*f_!, which need not be a categorical factorization or an isomorphism in general.

**Construction.**

1. Use the exact support kernel on the quasi-étale analytic tube site supplied by RD.4.
2. Apply the support functor before the analytic specialization pushforward and then the embedding-system pushforward.
3. Construct the special-fiber comparison by the adjunction map and preserve its direction.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.tubeProperSupport.kernel` (characterisation): The supported sheaf is the kernel of restriction to ]X∖U[.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.tubeProperSupport.whole` (simp): For U=X, f_! is the identity.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.tubeProperSupport.special_fibre_map` (compatibility): There is the source natural map F_!F\*Rs_\*→Rs_\*f_!, without a general isomorphism claim.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.tubeProperSupport.whole_space` (degenerate): Taking U=X recovers the unsupported complex.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.tubeProperSupport.empty_open` (degenerate): Taking U empty gives the zero support kernel.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.tubeProperSupport.wrong_order` (non-example): If the complement tube is nonempty and the coefficient sheaf is its structure sheaf, the section 1 restricts to 1 and does not belong to the kernel defining f_!.

**Acceptance.**

- For U=X the support kernel is the identity.

### Convergent monodromy triangles

`CR.6/convergent-monodromy-triangle` · theorem · part CR.5

For the relative and absolute convergent log complexes with the stated analytic proper support, right wedge by θ=dlog t yields ω_(U,X)[−1]→ω̃_(U,X)→ω_(U,X)→^N ω_(U,X), compatibly with the Frobenius factor p. Thus Nφ=pφN in the same convention as the crystalline embedding model. Apply the source exact support functor on tubes before taking derived pushforwards.

**Proof outline.**

1. Take the absolute-relative log differential short exact sequence on the embedding tube.
2. Apply the exact tube support functor and derived specialization/hypercover pushforward.
3. Identify the connecting map with the fixed N convention and Frobenius scaling.

**Acceptance.**

- For U=X and a strictly semistable fiber this recovers the unsupported convergent triangle.

<a id="n-cr-6-ramified-hk-base-change"></a>
### Ramified Hyodo–Kato base change

`CR.6/ramified-hk-base-change` · theorem · part CR.5

For a finite residue extension k′/k and log base k′^(d)→k^log given by ℕ→ℕ, 1↦d, d≥1, put N^(d)=N_raw/d on the HK complex of a model over k′^(d). For a base change Y′=Y×_{k^log}k′^(d), the rational comparison C_HK^(d)(Y′)≃C_HK(Y)⊗_{K₀}W(k′)[1/p] is (φ,N)-equivariant with this normalized N^(d). Without normalization raw monodromy scales by d. In characteristic p, this is not a claim that the d=p root map is log étale.

**Proof outline.**

1. Compare the standard log-base parameter under t↦t^d, so dlog t becomes d dlog t′.
2. Use rational log crystalline/log rigid base change in the semistable setting and divide the raw boundary by d.
3. Transport Frobenius and verify the normalized connecting diagram.

**Acceptance.**

- For d=1 it is unramified base change; for d>1 omitting the 1/d changes the monodromy diagram.

<a id="n-cr-6-stein-hk"></a>
### Hyodo–Kato cohomology of Stein curves

`CR.6/stein-hk` · construction · part CR.5

For a smooth semistable Stein curve with a semistable weak formal model and a Stein exhaustion by relatively compact dagger/semistable pieces U_i, define its overconvergent HK cohomology using the RD.4 log rigid complex and its continuous projective-limit cohomology interface. H¹_HK is a projective limit of finite-dimensional K₀-spaces, with its Fréchet topology and continuous φ,N. The required strictness and limit hypotheses belong to the analytic owner. This is not ordinary nonproper crystalline cohomology.

**Construction.**

1. Import the semistable weak formal and dagger exhaustion with the specified restriction maps.
2. Take the log rigid cohomology and use strict differential and inverse-limit results to identify it with the projective limit of finite-dimensional groups.
3. Endow it with the limit topology and continuous operators rather than a bare vector-space limit.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.steinHK.limit` (characterisation): The topology is the projective-limit topology on the finite-dimensional exhaustion groups.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.steinHK.operators` (structure): φ and N act continuously and satisfy Nφ=pφN.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.steinHK.exhaustion_independence` (functoriality): Cofinal admissible Stein exhaustions give canonically isomorphic spaces.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.steinHK.good_reduction_piece` (computation): A good reduction piece has N=0 and its ordinary rigid HK computation.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.steinHK.cofinal_exhaustion` (compatibility): Passing to a cofinal subsequence gives the same Fréchet space.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.steinHK.affinoid_warning` (characterisation): The constructed Stein HK space is Hausdorff: the intersection of all neighborhoods of zero is {0}. A vector space with a non-Hausdorff cohomology topology fails this condition.

**Acceptance.**

- The Stein curve model gives a separated Fréchet HK space; arbitrary affinoid classical HK need not share this property.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.6/stein-hk-comparison`](#n-cr-6-stein-hk-comparison): The separated Fréchet inverse limit and continuous operators are the domain of the completed C comparison; finite-level tower HK uses these spaces and their continuous transition maps.

<a id="layer-cr-7"></a>
## CR.7 — Coefficient and arithmetic interfaces

*Coverage in the CR.5 part: planned. 10 nodes, 3 planets.*

The layer exports the coefficient objects other roadmaps consume, as interfaces on the objects of CR.1, CR.3 and CR.5 and of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2: finite projective coefficient crystals with their evaluations and connections; filtered Frobenius coefficients, where filtration, Frobenius and monodromy are extra data with Griffiths transversality and Nφ = pφN; the evaluation of the contravariant Dieudonné crystal D(G) of R07.2 with F, V and base change, its variance and Tate twists on ℚ_p/ℤ_p and μ_{p^∞}, and the Grothendieck–Messing filtration; relative crystalline direct images as derived crystals, and proper smooth base change (Berthelot–Ogus Theorem 7.8); Gauss–Manin connections on cohomology sheaves under explicit local-freeness and base-change hypotheses, with horizontal base change; and the compatibility of all of them with divided powers. None of these interfaces constructs a crystal, a Dieudonné module or a filtration of its own. The three planets are coefficient crystals, the Dieudonné crystal interface and the Gauss–Manin connection.

**Still open in this layer.**

- Provide the R07.2 crystalline Dieudonné/Grothendieck–Messing construction and actual evaluation maps.
- Verify the CR.3 torsion/rank and completed base-change inputs for the stated Gauss–Manin degrees.
- Bind Dieudonné, Hodge exactness, direct-image and Gauss–Manin maps to the actual supplier constructions; add evaluation/F,V, dual-twist and horizontal base-change tests.

<a id="n-cr-7-finite-projective-coefficients"></a>
### Finite projective coefficient interfaces

`CR.7/finite-projective-coefficients` · construction · planet “Crystalline coefficients” · part CR.5

Import a finite locally free crystal F from CR.1, or a finite locally free log crystal from CR.5. At every compatible PD object T export the actual finite projective module F_T and coherent pullback isomorphisms; on a log PD-smooth embedding export its integrable quasi-nilpotent connection. Tensor, dual and End use evaluation-compatible maps. On a compatible p-adic tower require separated complete evaluations with the finite-level reductions specified; rational coefficients mean explicit inversion of p.

**Construction.**

1. Import the ordinary crystal and finite-projective categories rather than redefine them.
2. Package the evaluation and connection equivalences with their actual structural maps.
3. Check tensor/dual/base-change compatibility and retain the completed reductions in the p-adic interface.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.coefficientInterface.evaluate` (projection): Evaluation at T returns the finite projective O_T-module F_T.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.coefficientInterface.pullback` (equivalence): For a compatible PD map g, g\*F_T≅F_T′.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.coefficientInterface.tensor_dual` (compatibility): Evaluation and connection commute with tensor products and finite locally free duals.

**Unit tests.**

<a id="n-cr-7-filtered-frobenius-coefficients"></a>
### Filtered arithmetic coefficient interfaces

`CR.7/filtered-frobenius-coefficients` · construction · part CR.5

For a supplied finite locally free crystal with Frobenius linearization φ:F_S^\*F→F, export this actual horizontal map. If invertibility after p-inversion is needed, require it. A filtration on its de Rham evaluation is additional specified locally split data satisfying Griffiths transversality; a log monodromy map must be horizontal and obey Nφ=pφN. None of these structures is inferred from the word crystal. Twist F(r) multiplies φ by p^{−r} rationally and shifts Fil^i to Fil^{i+r}.

**Construction.**

1. Import the coefficient crystal with its specified Frobenius and filtration maps.
2. Transport them through evaluation, keeping σ-linearization and transversality.
3. Use the stated Tate twist convention to scale Frobenius and shift the filtration.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.arithmeticCoefficientInterface.frobenius` (projection): Export the horizontal linearization F_S^\*F→F.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.arithmeticCoefficientInterface.twist` (relation): On F(r), φ_r=p^{−r}φ and Fil^i(F(r))=Fil^{i+r}F.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.arithmeticCoefficientInterface.base_change` (functoriality): Compatible base change preserves the specified filtration, Frobenius and monodromy maps.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.arithmeticCoefficientInterface.twist_zero` (degenerate): Twist by zero is the original coefficient package.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.arithmeticCoefficientInterface.twist_minus_one` (computation): The twist F(−1) multiplies Frobenius by p and shifts the filtration by −1.
- `TauCeti.LogCrystalline.arithmeticCoefficientInterface.crystal_not_filtered` (non-example): On the same constant rank-one rational crystal, the filtrations Fil⁰=K, Fil¹=0 and Fil¹=K, Fil²=0 are distinct and both transverse; the underlying crystal does not determine one of them.

**Acceptance.**

- The Tate twist convention agrees with R06.2 and the standard R07.2 modules.

**Uses recorded for the API.**

- [`CR.7/dieudonne-variance-twist`](#n-cr-7-dieudonne-variance-twist): The specified Frobenius scaling and filtration shift identify the multiplicative Dieudonné module as the −1 twist; horizontal filtered maps feed the semistable comparison owner.

<a id="n-cr-7-dieudonne-variance-twist"></a>
### Dieudonné variance and Tate twists

`CR.7/dieudonne-variance-twist` · theorem · part CR.5

Over perfect k, the evaluated contravariant crystal agrees with the exact R07.2 modules: D(Q_p/Z_p)=W(k)e with Fe=e, Ve=pe (semilinearity understood), and D(μ_{p∞})=W(k)e with Fe=pe, Ve=e. Rationally the latter is K₀(−1) under φ_{D(r)}=p^{−r}φ_D, while the constant group gives K₀(0). Cartier duality agrees with D(G∨)≅D(G)∨(−1). Verify the horizontal evaluation maps and variance, not only the slopes.

**Proof outline.**

1. Evaluate the existing crystalline functor at the Witt PD thickening and compare to the standard modules already owned by R07.2.
2. Check Frobenius/Verschiebung and the contravariant group-map direction.
3. Apply Cartier duality and the declared twist convention to identify the rank-one rational modules.

**Acceptance.**

- Constant and multiplicative groups have slopes 0 and 1, and their duality uses twist −1.

### Grothendieck–Messing filtration interfaces

`CR.7/messing-filtration-interface` · comparison · part CR.5

For a nilpotent PD thickening S₀→S with p locally nilpotent and the nilpotent divided powers required by R07.2, export D(G₀)_S and its locally direct summand Hodge filtration. In the contravariant convention, on S₀ the exact sequence is 0→ω_{G₀}→D(G₀)_{S₀}→Lie(G₀∨)→0. The R07.2 Grothendieck–Messing theorem identifies lifts of G₀ with lifts of this filtration. This node exports the maps and compatibility; it does not reprove the classification or extend it to nonnilpotent PD ideals.

**Proof outline.**

1. Import the source-qualified R07.2 deformation theorem and its exact nilpotent-PD hypotheses.
2. Transport the evaluation and Hodge inclusion through the coefficient interface.
3. Verify base-change and duality compatibility of the actual inclusion and quotient maps.

**Acceptance.**

- For the constant group the Hodge submodule is zero; for the multiplicative group it is the full rank-one evaluation.
